question: What should I check before leaving for an Erasmus exchange?
expected_key_points: Wait for the Outgoing Mobility Office email before starting the host university application.
Respect the host university application deadlines.
Complete a Learning Agreement of at least 30 ECTS and obtain the required signatures.
Complete the OLS language evaluation if the teaching language is not the student's mother tongue.
Complete the required enrolment steps and upload the signed mobility contract through the mobility portal.
Arrange accommodation and check health insurance, passport validity and visa requirements.
answer:
Before leaving for an Erasmus exchange, you should check the following items based on the official guidelines:

- Check that your European health insurance card is valid for the whole mobility period https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2025/05/Checklist-Erasmus_EN.pdf (Last checked: 12.11.2026).
- Download the International SOS assistance app, follow the instructions received via email, and note that this is an assistance service rather than health insurance https://www.uni.lu/en/mobility/outgoing-student-mobility/erasmus/erasmus-before-study-exchange/ (Last checked: 12.11.2026), https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2025/05/Checklist-Erasmus_EN.pdf (Last checked: 12.11.2026).
- If you are a Luxembourgish student, report your trip to the MAEE for safety reasons https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2025/05/Checklist-Erasmus_EN.pdf (Last checked: 12.11.2026).
- Check your passport validity and visa requirements, as some partners require validity beyond your mobility period https://www.uni.lu/en/mobility/outgoing-student-mobility/erasmus/erasmus-before-study-exchange/ (Last checked: 12.11.2026).
- Verify that your bank details are up to date in the Guichet Etudiant and match the information on your mobility contract (if you receive an Erasmus+ grant) https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2025/07/08160616/Financement_Financial_-Erasmus_25-26_FR-EN.pdf (Last checked: 12.11.2026), https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2025/05/Checklist-Erasmus_EN.pdf (Last checked: 12.11.2026).
- Review your personal information on your mobility contract, and if your address is wrong and/or different from the one on the guichet etudiant, ensure the address given on the guichet etudiant is correct https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2024/10/FAQ-Erasmus-FR_DE_-EN_24-25.pdf (Last checked: 12.11.2026).

The provided sources do not cover any additional pre-departure checks beyond these points.

question: Which documents should I prepare for Erasmus registration?
expected_key_points: Prepare a Learning Agreement (LA or OLA) covering at least 30 ECTS.
Obtain the required signatures from the student, programme director and host institution.
Upload the signed mobility contract through the mobility portal.
Complete the OLS language evaluation if the teaching language is not the student's mother tongue.
answer:
Based on the provided official sources, various documents are needed for your Erasmus+ mobility and registration stages:

- Grant Agreement / Mobility Contract: A compulsory administrative document containing mobility information and grant details that must be signed before departure or during the first month of mobility (https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2025/07/08160616/Financement_Financial_-Erasmus_25-26_FR-EN.pdf, Last checked: 12.11.2026; https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2024/10/FAQ-Erasmus-FR_DE_-EN_24-25.pdf, Last checked: 12.11.2026).
- Learning Agreement (OLA or Word form): A learning agreement detailing your courses (minimum 30 ECTS for Bachelor students) (https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2025/05/Checklist-Erasmus_EN.pdf, Last checked: 12.11.2026; https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2024/10/Modification_Learning_Agreement_Erasmus_outgoing_students.docx, Last checked: 12.11.2026). If the host university does not use the Online Learning Agreement (OLA), the Word form for changes or the standard learning agreement format is used (https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2025/05/Checklist-Erasmus_EN.pdf, Last checked: 12.11.2026; https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2024/10/Modification_Learning_Agreement_Erasmus_outgoing_students.docx, Last checked: 12.11.2026).
- European Health Insurance Card: Must be valid for the whole mobility period (https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2025/05/Checklist-Erasmus_EN.pdf, Last checked: 12.11.2026).
- International SOS Assistance App instructions (https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2025/05/Checklist-Erasmus_EN.pdf, Last checked: 12.11.2026).
- MAEE report: Luxembourgish students must report their trip to the MAEE for safety reasons (https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2025/05/Checklist-Erasmus_EN.pdf, Last checked: 12.11.2026).
- Documents for the Fewer Opportunities top-up (if applicable): Depending on the specific case, this may include a doctor-completed form confirming a disability or severe/chronic illness, a household composition certificate and proof that children spent the mobility period abroad, or a residence permit indicating refugee status (https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2025/07/08160616/Financement_Financial_-Erasmus_25-26_FR-EN.pdf, Last checked: 12.11.2026).

Please note that documents required later during or after the exchange (such as the Certificate of Arrival, Certificate of End of Stay, or Transcript of Records) are handled during subsequent steps of the mobility process (https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2025/05/Checklist-Erasmus_EN.pdf, Last checked: 12.11.2026).

question: How can I check whether my courses will transfer as credits?
expected_key_points: Agree on the courses and their recognition through the Learning Agreement.
Use the Learning Agreement to record the courses and ECTS.
If courses change during mobility, update the Learning Agreement using Table A2.
Provide reasons for exceptional course changes.
Obtain the required signatures from the student, host institution and sending institution.
Credits agreed in the Learning Agreement and confirmed by the Transcript of Records are automatically recognised according to the form.
answer:
To check and ensure your courses will transfer as credits, you must complete and have your Learning Agreement approved by both your home institution (via your programme director and faculty mobility contact) and your host institution https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2024/02/FDEF-How-to-create-and-fill-out-my-Online-Learning-Agreement-OLA-FDEF.pdf (Last checked: 12.11.2026), https://www.uni.lu/fdef-en/study-abroad/ (Last checked: 12.11.2026). By signing the Learning Agreement or Online Learning Agreement (OLA), your home university agrees to validate the courses upon your return if they are completed successfully https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2024/02/FDEF-How-to-create-and-fill-out-my-Online-Learning-Agreement-OLA-FDEF.pdf (Last checked: 12.11.2026). 

The following steps and rules apply to credit transfer and validation:
- You must include courses for at least 30 ECTS in total https://www.uni.lu/en/mobility/outgoing-student-mobility/free-mover/ (Last checked: 14.11.2026), https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2024/02/FDEF-How-to-create-and-fill-out-my-Online-Learning-Agreement-OLA-FDEF.pdf (Last checked: 12.11.2026).
- If you make changes after arriving, you must update your Learning Agreement (using the changes section or "Apply changes" in the OLA) and have it re-approved by both universities https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2024/10/Modification_Learning_Agreement_Erasmus_outgoing_students.docx (Last checked: 12.11.2026), https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2024/02/FDEF-How-to-create-and-fill-out-my-Online-Learning-Agreement-OLA-FDEF.pdf (Last checked: 12.11.2026), https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2025/02/Checklist-Free-mover_SEMP_EN.pdf (Last checked: 14.11.2026). Enrolling in courses without approval risks them not getting validated even if you complete them successfully https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2024/02/FDEF-How-to-create-and-fill-out-my-Online-Learning-Agreement-OLA-FDEF.pdf (Last checked: 12.11.2026).
- Only credits from courses approved on the final Learning Agreement are validated, and the approved Learning Agreement must correspond to the Transcript of Records provided by the host university https://www.uni.lu/en/mobility/outgoing-student-mobility/free-mover/ (Last checked: 14.11.2026), https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2024/02/FDEF-How-to-create-and-fill-out-my-Online-Learning-Agreement-OLA-FDEF.pdf (Last checked: 12.11.2026). 
- For credit recognition, the host university must issue a Transcript of Records and send it directly to your faculty contact (e.g., Stephanie Anderson for FDEF) https://www.uni.lu/en/mobility/outgoing-student-mobility/free-mover/ (Last checked: 14.11.2026), https://www.uni.lu/fdef-en/study-abroad/ (Last checked: 12.11.2026), https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2025/02/Checklist-Free-mover_SEMP_EN.pdf (Last checked: 14.11.2026).

The provided sources do not detail course transfer rules for faculties other than the Faculty of Law, Economics and Finance (FDEF) or general credit transfer guidelines outside of the Learning Agreement and Transcript process.

question: How should I plan health insurance for studying abroad in Europe?
expected_key_points: Arrange adequate health insurance before travelling.
Know that International SOS provides free 24/7 assistance for mobility trips.
Understand that International SOS is not an insurance provider and does not replace health insurance.
answer:
To plan your health insurance for studying abroad in Europe, you should check that your European health insurance card (CNS) is valid for the whole duration of your stay abroad. This guidance is noted in the free-mover and Erasmus checklists (https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2025/02/Checklist-Free-mover_SEMP_EN.pdf, Last checked: 14.11.2026; https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2025/05/Checklist-Erasmus_EN.pdf, Last checked: 12.11.2026). Additionally, the Erasmus page advises you to get adequate health insurance and mentions that International SOS provides free 24/7 assistance for mobility trips, though it is an assistance app rather than an insurance provider (https://www.uni.lu/en/mobility/outgoing-student-mobility/erasmus/erasmus-before-study-exchange/, Last checked: 12.11.2026; https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2025/02/Checklist-Free-mover_SEMP_EN.pdf, Last checked: 14.11.2026; https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2025/05/Checklist-Erasmus_EN.pdf, Last checked: 12.11.2026).

The provided sources do not contain further details on specific additional insurance policies for European destinations beyond the CNS card and the general advice to get adequate coverage. For more comprehensive guidance or specific questions, please consult the University's Erasmus+ guidance or contact the relevant mobility office.

question: Which deadlines should I put in an Erasmus preparation checklist?
expected_key_points: Regularly check the university student email account for mobility instructions.
Ensure the European Health Insurance Card is valid before departure.
After arrival, obtain the signed and stamped Certificate of Arrival and upload it to the mobility portal.
Update the Learning Agreement within the first month after arrival if courses or ECTS change.
At the end of the exchange, obtain and upload the Certificate of End of Stay and the required Learning Agreement documents.
Complete the online mobility report.
After returning, provide the required Transcript of Records to the academic contact.
answer:
According to the official sources, there are no fixed calendar deadlines provided for most Erasmus preparation steps, but the following timing guidelines and recurring dates are mentioned:

Preparation timing: You should prepare for your mobility semester one academic year before departure https://www.uni.lu/en/?p=10573 (Last checked: 14.11.2026).

Study Abroad Day: The mandatory information session for Bachelor students takes place each year in November, on the second Thursday https://www.uni.lu/en/?p=10573 (Last checked: 14.11.2026).

Mobility contract: The mobility contract must be signed before your departure or during the first month of mobility https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2024/10/FAQ-Erasmus-FR_DE_-EN_24-25.pdf (Last checked: 12.11.2026).

Learning Agreement updates: If there are any changes in courses or ECTS, you must update your learning agreement within the month of arrival https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2025/05/Checklist-Erasmus_EN.pdf (Last checked: 12.11.2026). Host universities may also set their own deadlines https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2024/10/Modification_Learning_Agreement_Erasmus_outgoing_students.docx (Last checked: 12.11.2026).

End-of-stay documents and report: Departure documents are due at the end of the exam period https://www.uni.lu/en/?p=12305 (Last checked: 14.11.2026). The online participant report arrives automatically on your mobility contract's end-of-stay date https://www.uni.lu/en/?p=12305 (Last checked: 14.11.2026).

Grant payments: The first grant payment (70%) is issued at least 4 weeks after receipt of your mobility contract via the mobility portal, and the balance is paid at least 4 weeks after the compulsory end-of-stay documents are received https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2024/10/FAQ-Erasmus-FR_DE_-EN_24-25.pdf (Last checked: 12.11.2026).

The sources do not specify calendar dates for application deadlines or submission deadlines for every step.

question: When should I contact my home university coordinator during an exchange?
expected_key_points: Recognise that the programme director is responsible for recognising ECTS earned abroad.
Understand that credit recognition is based on the Learning Agreement signed before the exchange.
Recommend contacting the programme director or relevant faculty mobility contact about academic recognition or agreed courses, while identifying this as a recommendation.
answer:
During your exchange, you should stay in touch with your faculty's mobility contact person, your programme director, and the Outgoing Mobility Office https://www.uni.lu/en/?p=12305 (Last checked: 14.11.2026). Additionally, if some of the courses you chose do not run after you arrive, you must modify your Learning Agreement (PDF) or Online Learning Agreement (OLA) and get it approved https://www.uni.lu/en/?p=12305 (Last checked: 14.11.2026).

The provided official sources do not explicitly detail every other possible circumstance or schedule for contacting your home university coordinator during the active period of your exchange.
